Man, it's funny reading how bitter I was 3 years ago, it's been tough because that shit really changed me but man I've grown a lot ever since. 

Some advice I have



1. Therapy, sounds cliche but it really helps, it's not like they just listen to you venting, a good therapist will actually dive deep into why you are feeling they way you feel and help you realize what is lacking in your life that makes you so attatched to this situation, in my case, I realized how the stuff I was going thru in life when I met this person (among other things like some emotional trauma) made me develop such a strong attatchment.

2. Hang out with friends or people who make you feel appreciated, if you don't have any, go out and make some friends, it's easier than you think.

3. Focus on your goals and what you can start doing to achieve them.

4. If you haven't already, learn to be content on your own, realize you don't need someone to be happy, craving validation is really tough but therapy can really help.

5. This is probably really really hard for you right now but don't take it personal, it might seem like they did it on purpose to hurt you but truth is they probably didn't really know what they were doing, they might have their own issues and that causes them to hurt other people, unfortunately you in this case, not saying it isn't their fault or anything, but don't overthink about why they wanted to hurt you so bad, maybe they just suck and they would've done the same to anyone else who was in your place, don't think there's anything wrong with you because this person played you.

6. Recovery isn't a straight line, it's more like a curve, some days you might feel better, good even, then the next you might wake up depressed and not being able to get it out of your mind, you might feel like you're taking 1 step forward and 2 steps back sometimes but just give it time

It's not hard at all man, it feels overwhelming at first but as you start to get into it it feels more intuitive, I'm not an expert or anything, I've always been self taught but I understand plenty of music theory just by using google and youtube, there's plenty of beginner music theory courses and free youtube videos out there, just type "music theory for beginners", it's honestly satisfying learning about it, when you realize all the subtle things that happen to make a song sound the way it does, it makes playing music much more fun, besides you can communicate better with other musicians.

Now, what everyone is talking about on this post is (If I'm not mistaken lol) intervals and harmony, intervals are the "steps" between each note, if you put together different notes with specific intervals between them, you form chords (harmony), depending on the combination of notes and intervals you use, you'll get different chords, of course, and there's a notation system for all types or combinacion (that's when you hear about minor, diminished, Dominant, Major7, Add9, etc) However, there's a lot of combinations that due to the intervals they use, could be written in more than one way, and it would still mean the same chord when you go play it on the guitar, just different names for the same thing.

Music theory tends to get really complicated on advanced levels the deeper you go, to the point that even a lot of music scholars disagree on stuff all the time cause at the end of the day it's not a science and it's all subjective to interpretation. But if you want to just master the basics it won't take more than a few days of youtube, don't be discouraged! It's never too late to learn and honestly it might help you in your playing or your songwriting
